claim.location: Shipped reference output 858/Matlab/Dp/Drivers/experiments.out, block 'Ex. 5.1' (lines 133-138): 'I = 6.106434990872165e-02' printed after the driver line besselint(sqrt([2 3 5 7 11]),0,1) (experiments.m, Example 5.1). The Exact answer line in the same block is 6.106434990872167e-02; that closed value is in the driver as a literature value, and the check is against the code's own printed output, not against the exact answer.
claim.paper_value: I = 6.106434990872165e-02 (Ex. 5.1, shipped experiments.out; the code computes this integral with a = sqrt([2 3 5 7 11]), nu = 0, m = 1)
claim.metric: value of besselint(sqrt([2 3 5 7 11]), 0, 1) returned as I (first output)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped value agrees with the authors' closed value 6.106434990872167e-02 to about 2e-17, so the printed output is accurate to 1e-15 relative. A tolerance of 1e-10 absolute (about 2e-9 relative) allows for Octave against the authors' Matlab and for library differences in gamma and ellipke, and is far tighter than the 1e-2 relative precision the driver's own Example 7.4 requests. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one besselint call with five factors.
cost.data_size: None: the driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. Code licence is not stated in the archive README; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors' own shipped driver prints a computed infinite-range integral to 16 digits; the integral needs the full besselint algorithm to evaluate, so the value tests the old code on a modern interpreter, not a closed form.
